source.author: verg
source.text: Tum pater omnipotens, aliquem indignatus ab umbris mortalem infernis ad lumina surgere vitae, ipse repertorem medicinae talis et artis fulmine Phoebigenam Stygias detrusit ad undas.
source.text_original: Tum pater omnipotens, aliquem indignatus ab umbris / mortalem infernis ad lumina surgere vitae, / ipse repertorem medicinae talis et artis / fulmine Phoebigenam Stygias detrusit ad undas.
source.text_english: Then the almighty Father, indignant that a mortal should rise from the shadows below to the lights of life, himself, the discoverer of such healing and of such an art, hurled Phoebigena with his thunderbolt down to the Stygian waters.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Tum genitor vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_original: Tum genitor 'vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt / ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu / fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis / noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas / hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_english: Then our father tells us these ancient things and all things, once established, continue in their own order and remain fixed in the course of events from the beginning of the world; for there was not yet any blood of ours on any lands when I was granting destinies, and from this came my power to rule justly, when I was setting up different kings through the ages.
